title: composability-contracts-and-latency-bounded-fanout-playbook-2026
author: Elena Kim
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines composability contracts and operational guardrails for latency-bounded fanout across Redwood services. It prescribes the request/response surface, tracing and SLI obligations, configuration examples (circuit breakers, hedging, time budgets), and a rollout checklist for converting polyfanout endpoints into composable, observable primitives that meet end-to-end latency budgets.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Prevent unbounded request fanout from violating latency SLOs while preserving service composability and progressive feature rollout.
- Scope: Applies to all internal and customer-facing HTTP/gRPC/streaming services that may fan out to two or more downstream services. Includes hosted API, internal orchestration planes, and dedicated/private runtime proxies.
- Out of scope: Batch offline jobs (ETL, nightly retrain) and one-off admin scripts.

Definitions:
- Fanout: A single incoming request that synchronously invokes multiple downstream RPCs as part of fulfilling the response.
- Time budget: The maximum end-to-end latency allocated to a service (in ms) for a given request class.
- Budget reservation: Portion of a time budget reserved for specific downstream dependency classes (cache, inference, user-db).

Service contract requirements (must be included in service API spec):
1) Explicit time_budget_millis header or field on every request (integer). Example: time_budget_millis: 200
2) Max_concurrency_hint: integer hint for safe parallelism (default 1).
3) Causation and tracing: X-Request-ID (UUID), X-Trace-Id, span propagation using W3C Trace Context.
4) Idempotency key: required for any request that may be retried by proxies/clients.
5) Response envelope: { status, elapsed_ms, partial: boolean, errors: [] } (JSON).

Example API snippet (JSON contract):
{
  "request_headers": ["X-Request-Id", "traceparent", "time_budget_millis", "max_concurrency_hint", "x-idempotency-key"],
  "response_schema": {"status": "string", "elapsed_ms": "integer", "partial": "boolean", "errors": "array"}
}

Latency budgeting and SLO allocation:
- Default end-to-end SLO for interactive endpoints: p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 600ms.
- Allocation guidance (example for 250ms SLO):
  - Edge / ingress: 20ms
  - Orchestration layer: 30ms
  - Inference / compute: 150ms
  - Downstream DB/cache: 30ms
  - Observability & marshaling: 20ms
- Per-dependency caps are conservative starting points; teams must compute derived SLOs using the service's traffic signature.

Fanout patterns and allowed topologies (examples):
- Sequential (chain): Allowed when downstream latency budgets are well-known; prefer when shared state must be updated in order.
- Parallel bounded: Allowed up to max_parallel configured by policy (see table below). Must respect per-call timeouts and cancellation semantics.
- Aggregation streaming: Allowed with early-exit policy (return partial results if X% of downstreams timeout).

Topology safety table (default policy):
Service type | Typical max_parallel_calls | per-call timeout (ms) | rationale
Edge/ingress | 2 | 80 | Protect ingress CPU and guard worker pools
Orchestrator | 8 | 120 | Worker pool sizing for burst handling
Background-sync | 64 | 60000 | Background tasks tolerate long tail
Inference-coordinator | 4 | 300 | Bound GPU KV cache pressure

Operational controls (must be implemented):
- Time budget propagation: every intermediate service must decrement and honor time_budget_millis. If time_budget_millis <= 0, fail-fast with 504 and error code TIME_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED.
- Circuit breaker default config (YAML):
  circuit_breaker:
    failure_threshold: 0.25
    sample_window_ms: 60000
    min_requests: 20
    cooldown_ms: 120000
    half_open_max_calls: 5
- Hedging defaults: allowed only for read-only endpoints; max_hedges=1, hedge_delay_ms=30 (applied selectively).
- Cancellation: use context cancellation propagation (gRPC context, fetch AbortSignal).

Observability & telemetry obligations:
- Traces: all fanout-related spans MUST include attribute fanout.children = <number>. Root span should set budget_ms and budget_remaining_ms at start and on exit.
- Metrics (per service):
  - fanout_calls_total (labels: outcome, downstream_service, endpoint)
  - fanout_success_ratio (rolling 5m)
  - fanout_partial_responses_total
  - time_budget_exhaustions_total
  - downstream_latency_ms_bucket (histogram)
- Dashboards: Each service owning fanout logic must publish a 5-panel dashboard: incoming latency, fanout concurrency, partial response rate, budget exhaustion rate, top-5 slow downstreams.
- Alerts (recommended):
  - P99 latency > SLO by 50% sustained for 5m -> page oncall Backend SRE
  - time_budget_exhaustions_total rate > 0.5% over 10m -> create incident: likely fanout overload

Contract tests & CI enforcement:
- Contract-test harness should validate: header propagation, time_budget_decrement, circuit-breaker behavior, partial-response semantics.
- Add a lightweight synthetic runner in CI that exercises fanout topologies with simulated delays and asserts budget invariants. Example smoke command: 
$ ./tools/fanout-smoke --endpoint /v1/compose --budget 300 --downstreams 4 --delay 80

Rollout and migration checklist (for teams converting existing endpoints):
1) Draft API spec updates (include headers/time_budget). 2) Add budget propagation and failing behavior in local dev. 3) Implement tracing attributes and metrics. 4) Run contract-tests against a mock downstream harness. 5) Canary rollout at 1% traffic with increased sampling. 6) Monitor fanout_partial_responses_total & time_budget_exhaustions_total for 30m. 7) Gradual ramp every 24 hours with automated rollback if alarms fire.

Example runtime policy (JSON) to be consumed by the runtime router: 
{
  "route": "/v1/compose",
  "max_parallel": 6,
  "per_call_timeout_ms": 120,
  "aggregation_policy": "early_exit_quorum",
  "quorum_pct": 70
}

Design notes and rationale:
- Explicit time budgets avoid implicit blocking and make trade-offs measurable across teams.
- Bounded parallelism prevents head-of-line blocking in worker pools and reduces GPU KV cache thrash.
- Partial responses + clear envelope enable progressive UX while preserving correctness for idempotent operations.

Exemptions and special cases:
- Services requiring strong consistency for writes may request an exemption from parallel bounded defaults; exemption requires SRE review and a mitigation plan (retry budgets, compensating transactions).
- Third-party integrations that cannot be retrofitted must be isolated behind adapter services that translate to the contract.

Ownership and governance:
- Policy owner: Runtime Platform team (runtime-policy@redwood.ai).
- Enforcement: API review board approves exemptions; Eng-SRE enforces runtime defaults.
- Review cadence: Annual review or after any incident causing budget exhaustion.

Testing scenarios (recommended):
1) Slow downstream spike: simulate 30% of downstream instances adding +400ms latency; verify p95 stays within allocation or CI flags break.
2) Spike in parallel callers: create 10x concurrent client load and ensure max_parallel caps keep the service stable.
3) Network partition: verify that partial responses are returned and errors are annotated with error.type = "fanout_downstream_unavailable".

References and related pages:
- See request-priority-and-hinting-protocol-playbook-2026 for payload hint propagation.
- See slo-driven-runtime-contracts-and-rollback-playbook-2026 for runtime rollback triggers.

Appendix: sample instrumentation code (Node.js / Express)
// Middleware to validate and propagate time budget and tracing headers
function budgetMiddleware(req, res, next) {
  const incoming = parseInt(req.header('time_budget_millis') || '0', 10);
  const decrement = 10; // middleware overhead estimate
  const remaining = Math.max(0, incoming - decrement);
  res.setHeader('time_budget_remaining', String(remaining));
  if (remaining <= 0) return res.status(504).json({status: 'error', errors: ['TIME_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED']});
  req.timeBudget = remaining;
  next();
}

Contact and escalation:
- For questions or exemptions, open PR to runtime-policy with the tag "fanout-exemption" and notify Runtime Platform. For urgent incidents, page #runtime-slo-alerts and Eng-SRE oncall.
